preconditions.description: The number of test cases t is an integer between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= n <= 10**5 for n in [int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit() and int(line) <= 10**5])
preconditions.description: Each test case's length n is an integer between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(a) == n and all(1 <= x <= n for x in a) and len(set(a)) == n for a in [[int(x) for x in line.split()] for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit()])
preconditions.description: Each permutation is a list of n distinct integers between 1 and n inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(len(subseq) >= 1 for subseq in [line.split()[1:] for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip() and len(line.split()) > 1])
postconditions.description: Each subsequence has at least one element.

postconditions.expression: all(all(subseq[i] < subseq[i+1] for i in range(len(subseq)-1)) or all(subseq[i] > subseq[i+1] for i in range(len(subseq)-1)) for subseq in [line.split()[1:] for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip() and len(line.split()) > 1])
postconditions.description: Each subsequence is either strictly increasing or strictly decreasing.

postconditions.expression: all(all(x in subseq for x in a) for a, subseqs in zip([[int(x) for x in line.split()] for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip() and not line.strip().isdigit()], [[line.split()[1:] for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip() and len(line.split()) > 1] for _ in range(t)]))
postconditions.description: Every element of the permutation is included in exactly one subsequence.

postconditions.expression: all(len(subseqs) <= f(n) for n, subseqs in zip([int(line) for line in stdin.splitlines() if line.strip().isdigit()], [[line.split()[1:] for line in stdout.splitlines() if line.strip() and len(line.split()) > 1] for _ in range(t)]))
postconditions.description: The number of subsequences is at most f(n), where f(n) is the minimum integer k such that every permutation of length n can be partitioned into at most k monotonic subsequences.
